title: Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) Therapy
summary: Initial 12-week coverage of CPAP (HCPCS E0601) requires a diagnostic sleep test showing Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) or Respiratory Disturbance Index (RDI) >= 15 events/hour, or AHI 5-14.9 events/hour with documented excessive daytime sleepiness, hypertension, or ischemic heart disease.

sections.title: Coverage Criteria for Initial 12-Week Period
sections.content:
A single-level CPAP device (HCPCS E0601) is covered for adult patients with OSA when:
1. The patient had a face-to-face clinical evaluation prior to the sleep study.
2. The patient had a valid diagnostic sleep test (polysomnography or HSAT) showing:
   a. AHI or RDI >= 15 events per hour; OR
   b. AHI or RDI between 5 and 14.9 events per hour accompanied by documented excessive daytime sleepiness (ESS >= 10), impaired cognition, mood disorder, hypertension, or ischemic heart disease.
3. The patient and caregiver have received education on the use and maintenance of CPAP.

sections.title: Continued Coverage After 12 Weeks
sections.content: Continued coverage past 90 days requires documented compliance: usage >= 4 hours per night on 70% of nights during a consecutive 30-day period.

criteria.title: Face-to-Face Clinical Evaluation
criteria.description: Documented in-person face-to-face clinical evaluation with physician documenting sleep-related symptoms.
criteria.required_evidence: Clinical encounter note with history of sleep disturbance and physical exam.

criteria.title: Diagnostic Sleep Study with AHI Criteria
criteria.description: Sleep test documenting AHI/RDI >= 15 events/hr, OR AHI 5-14.9 events/hr with documented daytime sleepiness, hypertension, or cardiovascular comorbidity.
criteria.required_evidence: Sleep study report stating exact AHI/RDI number and accompanying symptoms if AHI < 15.
